thread.title: The China iPhone Sales Ban Will Spur Apple and Qualcomm to Settle, Say Analysts

author: Barron's
title: The China iPhone Sales Ban Will Spur Apple and Qualcomm to Settle, Say Analysts
text:
Photograph by Zhang Kaiyv Qualcomm 's court victory in China against Apple this week will likely spur the two parties to settle their dispute over patent royalties, according to Wall Street analysts.
On Monday, a Chinese intellectual-property court found Apple (ticker: AAPL) in violation of two of Qualcomm's ( QCOM ) patents and issued a preliminary injunction on sale of models from 2015's iPhone 6S through 2017's iPhone X in the country.
JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee reiterated his Overweight rating for Apple stock , predicting a deal between the two companies. He has a $266 price target for the smartphone maker.
"We believe the most likely outcome of the ruling and pending litigations are to drive a faster-than-earlier expected settlement between Apple and Qualcomm relative to ongoing litigation centered around compensation for Qualcomm's IP portfolio," he wrote on Tuesday.
Apple stock is down slightly on Tuesday, while Qualcomm shares rose 1.4%.
He expects the two parties to come to a settlement, but in the event the China sales ban of older iPhones does take effect, Chatterjee estimated it will hurt Apple's earnings per share by 50 cents per year.
https://asset.barrons.com/dj-mg/dice/barrons-staffpicks-2d590600-c862-4394-b9d3-66b48c376d60/inset.json
"However, we should highlight that stop-sale on older phones will be partly offset by substitution of newer phones," he wrote.
In similar fashion, Canaccord Genuity analyst T. Michael Walkley said the Chinese court ruling will be a catalyst for a resolution between the technology companies.
The "preliminary injunction against older iPhone models in China could be first step toward settling Apple royalty dispute," he wrote on Monday. "There are several ongoing legal and ITC [International Trade Commission] cases reaching later stages in the coming months that could facilitate Apple and Qualcomm finally reaching a resolution on the ongoing royalty disputes."
Walkley has a Buy rating for Qualcomm stock and a $75 price target for the shares.
